notes: HVS1 — Table 1 (T:p11-b0) enumerates the 21 retained unbound HVSs as HVS 1, 4–10, and 12–24; no HVS2 or HVS3 is identified in the supplied material. The other rows under “Possible Bound HVSs” in T:p11-b0/I:p11-b0 lack individual identifiers and are therefore not separate roster entries. HVS11 — The paper reclassifies HVS11 as a possible “bound HVS” (T:p6-b9); because it bears an HVS number and the text says “now classify,” it is listed as a follow-up of a previously identified candidate, not as one of the 21 unbound candidates. SDSS J115734.45+054645.58 — Included as follow-up because the paper re-observes this previously reported −359 km/s HVS-survey object and now identifies it as a log g≃5 white dwarf in a binary (T:p3-b5), retaining no unbound claim.

HVS1: Table 1 labels the heliocentric velocity column v_⊙; the text confirms this interpretation for new HVSs (e.g., HVS22 v_helio = 597.8 ± 13.4 km/s matches its table v_⊙ value), so HVS1's v_⊙ = 833.0 ± 5.5 km/s is recorded as radial_velocity. The table's v_rf = 675.0 km/s is a line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame velocity/minimum space velocity, not a total 3D speed. The (μ_α, μ_δ)_GC values in Table 1 are model-predicted proper motions for a Galactic center origin (Section 5), not measured present-day proper motions. No explicit RA, Dec, parallax, or heliocentric distance for HVS1 appears in the supplied materials; R_GC = 106 ± 14 kpc is Galactocentric distance. HVS1 is included among the 21 unbound HVSs, but no bound or unbound probability is reported.

HVS4: For HVS4, the table's v_rf = 551.5 km/s is a line-of-sight velocity in the Galactic rest frame, not a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity or a total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it was not recorded under the defined quantities. The table's (mu_alpha, mu_delta)_GC values are model predictions for a Galactic center origin, not measured proper motions; they are recorded with that condition.

HVS5: Table 1's v_⊙ column is treated as heliocentric radial velocity because the HVS22 value there matches the text's v_helio = 597.8 ± 13.4 km/s (T:p3-b8). For HVS5, Table 1 also reports v_rf = 650.1 km/s, but this is a line-of-sight Galactic-rest-frame velocity, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not entered as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No individual RA, Dec, parallax, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS5 in the supplied material.

HVS6: HVS6 has no reported right ascension, declination, parallax, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probability in the supplied material. Table 1's v_rf = 501.4 km/s is the line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame velocity, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The tabulated proper motions are predictions for a Galactic center origin, not measured proper motions.

HVS8: Table 1 reports v_rf = 408.3 km/s for HVS8 (T:p11-b0), but the paper defines v_rf as a line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame velocity, not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed; therefore no value was assigned to galactic_rest_frame_velocity. The (mu_alpha, mu_delta)_GC values in Table 1 are predicted proper motions for a Galactic center origin, not measured present-day proper motions.

HVS10: For HVS10, the supplied material gives no equatorial coordinates, parallax, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probability; Table 1 instead provides Galactocentric radius R_GC. The tabulated (µα, µδ)_GC values are predictions for a Galactic center origin, not measured proper motions (T:p8-b13, T:p11-b0). I record v_rf = 416.7 km/s as the reported Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity, noting that the paper states the full space motion can only be larger (T:p3-b4); it is not explicitly the total three-dimensional speed.

HVS13: HVS13 values are from Table 1 (T:p11-b0; I:p11-b0). The paper does not report RA/Dec, parallax, heliocentric distance, or bound/unbound probabilities for HVS13. The v_rf value is the line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame velocity rather than total three-dimensional speed, and the tabulated (mu_alpha, mu_delta)_GC values are predicted proper motions for a Galactic center origin, not measured proper motions.

HVS14: Table 1 at T:p11-b0 gives HVS14 v_rf = 409.4 km/s, but the paper describes v_rf as the Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity/minimum space velocity; at T:p3-b4 it states that because only radial velocity is measured, the full space motion can only be larger. Therefore this v_rf is not entered as the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed. The Table 1 proper motions are model predictions for a Galactic center origin, not measured proper motions.

HVS15: HVS15 is listed under the unbound HVSs in Table 1 (T:p11-b0), while the text (T:p6-b6) calls it a borderline case considered a likely HVS. The Table 1 v⊙ column is interpreted as heliocentric radial velocity because the HVS22 value in that column (597.8 ± 13.4 km/s) matches the text's stated v_helio for HVS22 (T:p3-b8). The proper motions recorded here are model predictions for a Galactic center origin from Table 1 and T:p8-b13, not measured proper motions. No right ascension, declination, parallax, or heliocentric distance is reported for HVS15 in the supplied material; the tabulated 67 ± 10 kpc is the Galactocentric radial distance R, not a heliocentric distance.

HVS16: HVS16 has no tabulated RA, Dec, parallax, observed proper motion, or bound/unbound probability in the supplied material. The proper-motion values are predictions for a Galactic center origin from T:p11-b0 and T:p8-b13, not measurements. The v_rf = 346.2 km/s value is the line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame component; because the paper states the full space motion can only be larger (T:p3-b4), it is recorded as a lower bound on the total Galactic rest-frame speed.

HVS18: HVS18 was identified from Table 1 row "18" (T:p11-b0; also visible in the image I:p11-b0). The table's v_rf column is the line-of-sight Galactic rest-frame velocity, not the total three-dimensional speed; the paper states the full space motion can only be larger. The proper motions in Table 1 are model predictions for a Galactic center origin, not measured values. No equatorial coordinates, parallax, or direct heliocentric distance are reported for HVS18 in the supplied material, and I did not compute a distance from the tabulated g0 and M_g.

HVS19: For HVS19, no heliocentric distance, parallax, right ascension, or declination is reported in the supplied material. The Table 1 entry at T:p11-b0 gives v_rf = 492.0 km/s, but v_rf is a Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight velocity rather than a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity or the total 3D Galactic-rest-frame speed, so it is not entered under those quantities. The proper motions at T:p11-b0 are model predictions for a Galactic center origin (see T:p8-b13), not measurements.

HVS21: HVS21 is listed among the 21 unbound HVSs in Table 1 (T:p11-b0), with v_rf = 391.9 km/s, R_GC = 113 ± 21 kpc, and predicted Galactic-center-origin proper motion (μ_α, μ_δ)_GC = (-0.18, -0.45) mas/yr. The paper reports no heliocentric distance, parallax, right ascension, declination, or measured proper motion for HVS21. The table's (μ_α, μ_δ)_GC values are predicted proper motions for a Galactic center origin (T:p8-b13), not measured present-day proper motions, so they are not recorded. The paper states v_rf is a Galactic rest-frame radial/line-of-sight velocity and that the full space motion can only be larger (T:p3-b4); it is therefore not the total three-dimensional Galactic rest-frame speed and is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No numeric bound or unbound probability is reported.

HVS22: HVS22 is SDSS J114146.45+044217.29 (T:p1-b4, T:p3-b8). The paper does not tabulate separate equatorial coordinates or a parallax for HVS22; the SDSS designation encodes coordinate-like numbers but the authors do not report them as separate RA/Dec quantities. The proper motions in Table 1 and at T:p8-b13 are predictions for a Galactic center origin, not measured proper motions.
